test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize in which year for her debut novel 'The God of Small Things'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Arundhati Roy** was awarded the prestigious **Booker Prize** in the **year 1997**.

• The award was conferred for her **debut novel**, **'The God of Small Things'**, which achieved global critical and commercial success.

• She holds the distinction of being the **first Indian citizen** to win this international literary award, bringing significant recognition to **Indian English literature**.

• The novel is set in **Ayemenem**, a village in the **Kottayam district** of **Kerala**, and captures the complex social and political atmosphere of the **1960s**.

• The story focuses on the lives of **fraternal twins**, **Rahel** and **Esthappen**, and explores deep-seated themes of **caste discrimination**, **communism**, and the **'Love Laws'** that dictate social boundaries in **India**.

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Arundhati Roy** was born on **November 24, 1961**, in **Shillong**, **Meghalaya**, to a **Syrian Christian** mother and a **Bengali Hindu** father.

• Beyond her literary achievements, she is a prominent **political activist** and **essayist** who has spoken extensively on **human rights**, **environmental justice**, and the impacts of **globalization**.

• Her second major novel, **'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness'**, was published in **2017**, nearly **20 years** after her debut, and was longlisted for the **Man Booker Prize**.

• She won the **National Film Award** for **Best Screenplay** in **1989** for the film **'In Which Annie Gives It Those Ones'**.

• Some of her notable non-fiction works include **'The Algebra of Infinite Justice'**, **'Power Politics'**, and **'War Talk'**, which critique **neo-imperialism** and **state policies**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Booker Prize** was established in **1969** and is one of the world's most famous literary prizes, awarded annually for the best novel written in **English** and published in the **UK** or **Ireland**.

• Other **Indian** or **Indian-origin** authors who have won the prize include **V.S. Naipaul** (**1971**), **Salman Rushdie** (**1981**), **Kiran Desai** (**2006**), and **Aravind Adiga** (**2008**).

• In **1993**, **Salman Rushdie's** **'Midnight's Children'** was awarded the **'Booker of Bookers'** to commemorate the **25th anniversary** of the prize.

• Winning the **Booker Prize** carries a cash reward of **£50,000** and typically leads to a massive increase in international **book sales** and **translation** into multiple **languages**.

• The prize is currently managed by the **Booker Prize Foundation** and is sponsored by **Crankstart**, a charitable foundation.
